artists.biography: "Solstice"  is a prog rock band from Milton Keynes, England and part of the '80s progressive revival in the UK. Similar in style to such bands as Marillion, Twelfth Night, Pendragon, and IQ, they released four studio albums: "Silent Dance" ('84), "New Life" ('93), "Circles" ('96), "Spirit" (2010); a live album, and a compilation. Their first three studio albums and were remastered and reissued with bonus tracks as 'Definitive Editions' in 2007. "The Cropredy Set" (live) was also re-released as a CD+DVD set.

perplexity.description:
Solstice's eighth studio album, Clann, was released on April 4, 2025, through ProgRock.com's Essentials label. The album continues the UK progressive rock band's tradition of blending melodic songwriting with atmospheric textures and intricate arrangements. Musically, Clann features a mix of expansive, multi-part compositions and more intimate, homespun moments, anchored by the band's signature use of layered keyboards, dynamic guitar work, and rich vocal harmonies. Standout tracks like the 13-minute "Twin Peaks" showcase Solstice's prog roots, while the bonus track "Earthsong" revisits material from their 1984 debut, highlighting their evolving yet consistent sound.

Clann marks the latest chapter in Solstice's long-running discography, following their 2022 release Light Up and completing a trilogy that began with Sia (2020). The album has been praised for its engaging blend of classic and contemporary progressive rock, with critics noting its charm and inclusivity. Reviews have highlighted the album's ability to both honor the band's legacy and reach new listeners, with Get Ready to Rock! calling it "utterly engrossing" and commending its memorable performances and thoughtful songwriting. The release was supported by a UK tour, further cementing Solstice's active presence in the modern prog rock scene.
